items.title: Bangladesh garment workers, police clash in fresh wage protest
items.description:
Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed.
Protesters hurled bricks, torched vehicles and blocked the main highway between capital Dhaka and key financial district Mymensingh as demonstrations demanding higher wages turned violent.
The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, producing clothes for major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss.

items.title: Pakistan's fast bowling masterclass bundles Sri Lanka out for 98 in second Test
items.description:
Pakistan’s fast bowlers produced a devastating display to dismiss Sri Lanka for just 98 in 35.3 overs on the opening day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday, exploiting the movement on offer to leave the visitors with little chance of building a competitive total.
After winning the toss and opting to field, Pakistan reduced Sri Lanka to 36-5 in the morning session before completing the job shortly after lunch, taking the last four wickets for just 13 runs in 6.3 overs.

items.title: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to support Pakistan’s federal pension reforms
items.description:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Tuesday approved a $500 million results-based loan to help Pakistan reform its federal civil pension system, the Manila-based lending agency said in a statement.
The reforms will help contain rising pension-related fiscal pressures, strengthen pension system sustainability, and expand fiscal space for development and social spending, according to the statement.

items.description:

items.title: 796 Afghans arrested in first week of November
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Law-en­forcement agencies arres­ted 796 Afghan nationals during the first week of November from Balochis­tan, Khyber Pakhtun­kh­­wa, Punjab and Islamabad.
